body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

ActivityConfig(summary=...) takes a static string, so every invocation of a given activity shows the same text in the Temporal UI. For invoke_model and tool calls in ADK workflows, the useful context — which agent, what arguments, what stage of reasoning — varies per call. There's currently no way to generate summaries from call-time context.

### Describe the solution you'd like

Some mechanism for generating summaries dynamically based on the request/arguments at call time. For TemporalModel, this means access to the LlmRequest; for activity_tool, access to the tool arguments. Open to whatever API shape makes sense — callback, format string, template, etc.

### Additional context

This feedback is based on the Python SDK's ADK integration, but the same pattern applies to other SDK implementations. We subclassed TemporalModel and extended activity_tool to build per-call summaries like [#6] Fleet Agent — LLM reasoning on fleet data and tool summaries from arguments. Happy to share our implementation as a reference.
This pattern was identified while working on the ADK/Temporal NEXT demo: https://github.com/temporal-community/ice-cream-fleet-demo

Tracking: AI-60 (https://temporalio.atlassian.net/browse/AI-60)

comments.body:
Dynamic per-call activity summaries are a significant quality-of-life improvement for multi-agent workflows — static summaries make the Temporal UI nearly useless for tracing incidents when 20 agents are all showing "invoke_model".

The callback/format-string approach you suggest is the right direction. A few considerations for the implementation:

**Trust tier as a first-class summary token.** Beyond agent name and arguments, including the agent trust tier in the summary (T0-T4 or a trust score bucket) makes security-relevant incidents immediately visible in the timeline without opening individual activity details. An operator investigating an incident can scan for "T3 agent" activities in the timeline to identify where elevated-privilege actions occurred.

**Argument redaction for sensitive parameters.** Dynamic summaries that include tool arguments are useful but need care — if a tool argument contains an auth token, API key, or PII, it should be redacted before inclusion in the summary (which may be logged or displayed). A `summary_safe_args` filter on the tool definition (analogous to `required=False` on `@ToolParam`) would let tool authors declare which arguments are safe to include in activity summaries.

**Correlation with behavioral trust.** If the dynamic summary includes a consistent `agent_id` token, activity summaries become a behavioral audit trail — you can query Temporal history for all activities by a specific agent identity and compute metrics like per-agent error rate, cost, and latency without a separate observability layer. This is the prerequisite for trust scoring from Temporal data.

title: [Feature Request] Support dynamic per-call activity summaries in TemporalModel and activity_tool
